cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the saints in Ephesus (Ephesians 1:1), and he's just written that in all things we will grow up into Christ Himself (Ephesians 4:15). Now he gets serious. He insists in the Lord that they must no longer walk as the Gentiles do, in the futility of their thinking.
Paul says their understanding is darkened, and they're alienated from the life of God. Friend, I lived in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS, so believe me, dark is no way to live.

cards.question: Paul says the Gentiles are alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance in them. What is that ignorance due to?

cards.text: And Paul keeps going. Having lost all sense of shame, they've given themselves over to sensuality, for the practice of every kind of impurity.

cards.question: Paul says the Gentiles have given themselves over to practice every kind of impurity. What else does he say they have?
Then Paul turns to the believers in Ephesus. True or false: Paul says the Gentiles' way of living is not the way the believers came to know Christ.
Paul says the believers heard of Christ and were taught in Him. What was that teaching in keeping with?

answers.text: The truth that is in Jesus

cards.text: Then Paul spells out what they were taught, and it comes in three steps, like a recipe card. And I LOVE a short recipe card, friend, because the long ones always end with me covered in flour.

cards.question: Step one: Paul says the believers were taught to put off their former way of life. What does he call it?
Paul says the old self is being corrupted by its desires. True or false: he calls those desires honest.

cards.text: So you put it OFF, like a stained old work shirt. Not "I'll patch it," not "one more season," just OFF.

cards.question: Step two: Paul says the believers were taught to be renewed in the spirit of their ___.

cards.text: Step three, and here's the good part: put on the new self. And this time it's not that stained old work shirt, friend, it's brand NEW with the tags still on.

cards.question: Paul says the new self is created to be like ___ in true righteousness and holiness.

cards.text: Now Paul gets practical, starting with the mouth. Each of them must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to his neighbor.

cards.question: Why does Paul say each believer must speak truthfully to his neighbor?

answers.text: We are all members of one another
We will all stand before the Lord
Our words are weighed by God

cards.text: Lying to your neighbor is like your left hand lying to your right hand about who ate the last cookie: you share a STOMACH, friend. Next up, anger, and Paul quotes a short line about it.

cards.question: Paul quotes a short line about anger. True or false: the line tells the believers never to be angry.
The line is "Be angry, yet do not sin." Then Paul puts a deadline on anger. What is it?

answers.text: Don't let the sun set on it

cards.text: Sundown, friend: your anger works the DAY shift only, then it CLOCKS OUT. And Paul adds one more line.

cards.question: Paul adds: do not give the ___ a foothold.

cards.text: Then Paul speaks to anyone who has been stealing. He must steal no longer, and must work, doing good with his own hands.

cards.question: Paul gives the former thief a reason to work with his own hands. What is it?

answers.text: To have something to share with the one in need
To pay back everyone he ever stole from
To earn back his good name around town

cards.text: From taking stuff to giving stuff away, friend, that's not turning over a new leaf, that's a whole new TREE. Then Paul's back to the mouth: no unwholesome talk.

cards.question: Paul says let no unwholesome talk come out of the believers' mouths. What kind of talk should come out instead?

answers.text: Only what is helpful for building up
Only what shows how much you know

cards.question: True or false: Paul says helpful talk brings grace to those who listen.
Paul tells the believers not to grieve the Holy Spirit of God. True or false: he says the believers were sealed in the Spirit for the day of redemption.

cards.text: Then Paul clears the counter. Bitterness, rage, anger, outcry, slander and every form of malice: get rid of ALL of it.
Last line, and it's the sweet one: be kind and tenderhearted to one another, and forgive each other. After years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, I am NOT starting a new drawer full of grudges.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers to forgive each other. How does he say they should do it?

answers.text: Just as in Christ God forgave them
As each one confesses his sin
Seven times and then no more
